The National Superannuation Fund (Nasfund) had a highly successful weekend at the 63rd Morobe Show. We brought our services directly to the people, giving hundreds of hard-working Papua New Guineans instant access to their superannuation accounts.

Superannuation is a long-term savings plan designed to provide income during retirement. It offers financial benefits through regular contributions and long-term investment growth.

To grow your Nasfund superannuation, actively contribute regularly, whether through employer contributions or voluntary top-ups, to boost your retirement savings.

To minimize tax on your Nasfund superannuation payout, keep your savings invested for at least 15 years. This reduces your exit tax to 0%, compared to higher rates for earlier withdrawals, while also maximizing your savings through compound growth.

National Superannuation Fund Ltd or Nasfund is an accumulation fund and was the first Approved Superannuation Fund to be licensed by the Central Bank under the Superannuation (General Provisions) Act 2000 in 2002.

Eda Supa is for anyone who is earning some form of income and wants to save in a superannuation environment, farmers, sole traders and small business owners.

Nasfund's investee companies are carefully selected to align with the fund's strategy of delivering consistent returns, ensuring sustainable growth, and maximizing value for its members.

PORT MORESBY, National Superannuation Fund Limited (Nasfund) has been delivering its Superannuation (Supa) Education Sessions in schools across PNG since 2024 as part of its commitment to preparing young Papua New Guineans for their future financial journey.

The program is a superannuation education and awareness initiative designed to educate students to understand superannuation, retirement savings and personal financial planning.

The initiative equips participants with essential superannuation education, including how superannuation works, understanding the role of Nasfund, the importance of starting to save early, strategies for growing retirement savings and the value of making informed financial decisions throughout life.

As part of this ongoing initiative, Nasfund Member Experience Manager, Melisha Sindiwan, conducted three Supa Education sessions over the past two weeks at Port Moresby Grammar School, providing Grade 12 students with a practical introduction to superannuation and long-term financial planning.

The sessions were very engaging and focused on building awareness around superannuation education, encouraging students to begin thinking about their financial planning well before they enter the workforce. Students were introduced to the basics of superannuation, the role it plays in securing finances and retirement savings, and the benefits of establishing savings habits.

This marks the third consecutive year that Nasfund has partnered with Port Moresby Grammar School to deliver the Supa Education program under school enrichment program for grade 12s, reinforcing the Fund's commitment to investing in financial literacy and empowering future generations with the knowledge needed to make sound financial decisions.

Speaking on the importance of the program, Port Moresby Grammar School Director Curriculum for Senior School, Brenda Kekeao, said the Supa Education sessions align closely with the school's future financial planning module.

"For this module, we actually looked at other organisations, but the school chose Nasfund because of the long-standing relationship the school has with the company," Ms Kekeao said.

"From these sessions, we hope this will help educate students about their future financial planning."

LAE, MOROBE PROVINCE | The National Superannuation Fund (Nasfund) had a highly successful weekend at the 63rd Morobe Show. We brought our services directly to the people, giving hundreds of hard-working Papua New Guineans instant access to their superannuation accounts.

Many of our members work in areas like the 4 Mile to 9 Mile corridor and find it difficult to visit a branch during normal working hours. To help, we turned our show stall into a fully operational service hub.

Over the two days, members could easily print instant ID cards, update their account details, register online, merge accounts, check balances, ask about housing advances, and print statements.

The biggest highlight was our rapid, on-site ID printing. Members took photos, updated their information, and walked away with their official Nasfund ID cards in just minutes.

Member Apolos Agita praised the team's efficiency, saying, “I really appreciate that I got served and received my ID card instantly.”

Xena Eileen Usu, a contributor for over 20 years, was also thrilled with the quick service. She noted how much Nasfund's discount partners have helped members over the years.

Events like the Morobe Show are a great way for us to connect with members face-to-face, especially since our branches can be far from where they live and work. The massive turnout at our booth shows just how much members need access to these services outside of regular business hours.

Nasfund CEO Rajeev Sharma thanked everyone for visiting and reminded members to keep their records current. “We encourage you to update your details, especially if you haven't filled out a form yet,” he said.

To continue reaching busy workers, Nasfund invites Lae employers to arrange free workplace presentations. This allows staff to access essential superannuation services right at their job sites. HR teams can easily book a visit by emailing customerserviceslae@nasfund.com.pg .

Central Province: In our society, service delivery can be very difficult to reach some of the most remote parts of the country. With Nasfund's Member Service Booths, we can reach some members and this week we attended to more than 100 members of the Seventh Day Adventist (SDA) Pastors Central Papua Conference at Mt Diamond in Central.

Nasfund team attending to participants of the SDA Pastors Central Papua Conference at Mt Diamond in Central last week.

Speaking on behalf of the members, Tubuseria Village, SDA Church Pastor Jacob Mavo said having the Nasfund Service Booth team stationed at the conference venue was a very "good idea".

"From this engagement, pastors have now realized that we do not utilize well some of the services you provide, especially the voluntary contributions platform, " Mavo said.

"Our church has been really great especially in building our retirement savings and we are very blessed."

Mavo said other products like the housing advance product should also be utilized because pastors housing has been a very big issue within the church.

He thanked Nasfund for bringing their essential services like helping members to log in to their online platforms, issuance of Eda Supa forms, providing member detail update forms and attending to general enquiries.

9-mile Ridge in Port Moresby SDA church pastor Samuel James said Nasfund's mobile service booth at the conference this week was a great way to serve their members.

"We have pastors who contribute with Nasfund but have come from very inland parts of Central but they were given the service here and at their doorstep," he said,
